thesis: Sincere repentance (with prayer and zakah) turns former enemies into brothers in religion, while renewed oath-breaking joined to attack on the deen exposes its perpetrators as leaders of kufr who must be confronted.

flags.quote: Qatadah, Mujahid and as-Suddi name specific Quraysh leaders.
flags.issue: Position correct, sharpening loose. Tabari 16521/16522/16526 (Qatadah) and 16523 (Mujahid) do name individuals (Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, Umayyah b. Khalaf, Suhayl b. 'Amr, 'Utbah b. Rabi'ah). As-Suddi (16524) says only 'هؤلاء قريش' — he assigns the ayah to the historical Quraysh treaty-breakers but names no leaders. Right camp, over-specified.

flags.quote: And Qatadah's own report condemns exactly the misuse the Khawarij made of it, turning a verse about treaty-breakers against the people of the qiblah.
flags.issue: Qatadah's transmitted words (16526) are 'وليس والله كما تأوّله أهل الشبهات والبدع والفِرَى على الله وعلى كتابه'. The identification of those people as the Khawarij, and of the misuse as fighting ahl al-qiblah, is Mahmud Shakir's editorial footnote in the same fetched edition, not the athar itself. Substance is in the fetched text; the file folds footnote into report.

flags.quote: Hudhayfah and 'Ali are reported saying that the people of this ayah have not yet been fought at all
flags.issue: Both attributions verify, but not from the same source. Hudhayfah's 'ما قوتل أهل هذه الآية بعدُ' is in al-Tabari (16527-16529) and Ibn Kathir; 'Ali appears only in Ibn Kathir ('A similar statement was reported from 'Ali bin Abi Talib'). The paragraph is framed as al-Tabari's record, and the fetched Tabari text carries no 'Ali report. Agentless 'are reported' softens it.

notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. The added section 'Where the commentators divided' supplies exactly what the batch2 read demanded: the ikhtilaf over who a'immat al-kufr are (specific-Quraysh camp vs Hudhayfah's 'not yet fought'), the anti-Khawarij caveat, Ibn Kathir's generalizing reading and his contested ruling on cursing the Messenger, and a tadabbur-vs-fatwa line. Ibn Kathir's 'this Ayah is general' and the cursing-the-Messenger ruling both verify verbatim in the fetched text; al-Tabari's 'على اختلاف بينهم في المعنيِّين بأئمة الكفر' verifies the claim that a dispute is recorded. The section does NOT adjudicate — it says 'the safest thing a reader can carry away is the disagreement itself' and adds 'nothing here identifies any person or group living now, and rulings belong to qualified scholars', which also mitigates the batch2 second flag about universalizing the command into a present-tense lesson. Three minor source-precision imprecisions logged above; none misassigns a position to the wrong authority.

thesis: A spoken word of kufr remains real before Allah even when denied under oath afterward, yet the door of repentance is still held open before final turning away.

flags.quote: Al-Tabari opens his treatment of 9:73 with the phrase that should govern how anyone reads it: *wa-khtalafa ahl al-ta'wil fi sifat al-jihad*
flags.issue: Phrase verifies verbatim ('واختلف أهل التأويل في صفة الجهاد') but it is Tabari's second move, not his opening — he first glosses 'jahidi al-kuffara' as 'بالسيف والسلاح'. Tabari also scopes the dispute specifically to jihad against the munafiqin ('الذي أمر الله نبيه به في المنافقين'), which the file's ellipsis drops.

flags.quote: the dominant classical readings explicitly refuse to treat the two groups alike
flags.issue: Defensible by count (Ibn 'Abbas x2, ad-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, plus Muqatil/ar-Rabi' in Ibn Kathir, vs Ibn Mas'ud alone), but the section omits that al-Tabari's own tarjih goes the other way: 'وأولى الأقوال في تأويل ذلك عندي بالصواب، ما قال ابن مسعود'. Mitigated by the file presenting Ibn Mas'ud's view first (so both poles are visible) and by its next paragraph reproducing Tabari's own qualification about outward profession.

notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED — including the critical one. Every attribution in 'The word the commentators argued about' checks out against the fetched tafsir: Ibn Mas'ud's four-step sequence matches Tabari 16961 exactly ('بيده، فإن لم يستطع فبلسانه، فإن لم يستطع فبقلبه، فإن لم يستطع فليكفهرَّ في وجهه'); Ibn 'Abbas (16962/16963) and ad-Dahhak (16964) give sword-for-kuffar / tongue-for-munafiqin; al-Hasan (16965) and Qatadah (16966) give hudud; al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar both read 'بالسيف' vs 'باللسان والحجة' word for word. The second paragraph's fiqh distinction is likewise grounded — Tabari's own discussion states that whoever professes Islam outwardly has blood and property protected and that 'وتوكَّل هو جلّ ثناؤه بسرائرهم، ولم يجعل للخلق البحثَ عن السرائر' — and al-Julas's sincere repentance is Ibn Kathir's ('who, they claim, repented and his repentance was sincere'), correctly hedged as 'is reported to have'. The tadabbur-vs-fatwa line is present ('The second is a matter of fiqh, and belongs to scholars'). No adjudication: positions are reported, and the one leaning sentence is hedged with 'on those readings'. Note that the earlier body line the batch2 read quoted ('The command joins outward and inward enemies, then adds severity') is unchanged, but the new section explicitly complicates it, which is the repair that was asked for.

thesis: The most dangerous spiritual state is not loud rebellion but the soul settling heavily into earth when Allah calls it to rise, because Allah can punish and replace the reluctant without His mission suffering.

flags.quote: All four commentaries anchor these two ayahs to a specific moment: the expedition to Tabuk.
flags.issue: False for al-Muyassar. Its gloss on 9:38 ('اخرجوا إلى الجهاد في سبيل الله لقتال أعدائكم') and on 9:39 ('إن لا تنفروا أيها المؤمنون إلى قتال عدوكم') names no campaign at all — no Tabuk, no occasion. Three of four carry it (al-Tabari 'وذلك غزوة رسول الله ﷺ تبوك', Ibn Kathir 'the battle of Tabuk', al-Jalalayn 'غزوة تبوك'), which is exactly the list the file's own very next sentence gives. The 'all four' opener is contradicted by the file's own enumeration and asserts a source-agreement that the fetched text does not support.

flags.quote: Mujahid's reports place it in the summer mobilisation that followed the conquest, when the journey was long, the season was hard, and the harvest was ready.
flags.issue: Two of three details verify in Mujahid (Tabari 16719/16720): 'أمروا بغزوة تبوك بعد الفتح... أمروا بالنَّفير في الصيف، حين خُرِفت النخل، وطابت الثمار، واشتَهُوا الظلال، وشقّ عليهم المخرج' — summer after the conquest, harvest ready, hard season. 'The journey was long' is not in either Mujahid report; his phrase is 'شقّ عليهم المخرج' (setting out was hard on them). Distance/heat language belongs to al-Jalalayn ('عُسْرَة وشِدَّة حَرّ') and Qatadah (16723, 'في لَهَبَان الحرِّ في غزوة تبوك قِبَل الشأم'), not Mujahid.

flags.quote: This is one of the Qur'an's most accurate descriptions of the spiritual lethargy that appears when obedience gets costly.
flags.issue: Carried over unchanged from the batch3 read — unverifiable superlative, hedged by 'one of the'. Not part of the repair; logged for continuity.

notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED, BUT A NEW MISATTRIBUTION WAS INTRODUCED. The batch3 fix was specified as a Tabuk-context paragraph plus a tadabbur-vs-fatwa note, and 'The campaign this was revealed about' delivers both: the Tabuk anchor is now explicit, al-Tabari's Arabic is quoted correctly, the inward reading is made visible rather than silent ('the move should be visible rather than silent'), and the line 'This is a tadabbur, not a fatwa' is present. It does not adjudicate anything. The blocking problem is the opening sentence's 'All four commentaries' — al-Muyassar carries no occasion-of-revelation for either ayah, so the section overstates its own source agreement by one, and does so in the very sentence establishing the repair's authority. Fix is one word: 'Three of the four commentaries' (or name them), plus dropping 'the journey was long' from the Mujahid attribution or reattributing it to al-Jalalayn/Qatadah. Separately, not a flag but worth knowing for any future pass: al-Tabari records a real ikhtilaf on 9:39 that this file does not mention — 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri held the ayah abrogated by 9:122, and Tabari rejects the naskh claim ('ولا خبرَ بالذي قال عكرمة والحسن... يجب التسليم له'), arguing instead that the nafir obligation binds those actually summoned. That is the live dispute on this mobilization command.
